subject: nondeterminism-and-environmental-effects

models.name: CompCert 3.18
models.environment_boundary: external calls and volatile accesses emit observable events; external-call semantics is relational
models.environment_instantiation: coinductive deterministic world constrains I/O and volatile responses
models.nondeterminism_representation: multiple derivable program behaviors; environment responses are one explicitly identified source
models.observations: finite/infinite traces plus termination, silent divergence, reactive divergence, or going wrong
models.comparison_relation: forward/backward simulation over behaviors; behavior_improves accounts for source going-wrong prefixes
models.key_distinction: a deterministic external world is an additional assumption, not the general external-call semantics

models.name: Interaction Trees
models.environment_boundary: uninterpreted visible events with response-dependent continuations
models.environment_instantiation: event handlers interpret events as monadic actions
models.nondeterminism_representation: not the paper's dedicated internal-choice primitive; effects remain abstract until interpretation
models.observations: event structure, return values, and potentially nonterminating interaction
models.comparison_relation: equational theory up to weak bisimulation
models.key_distinction: effect signature and handler separate computation from environment semantics

models.name: Choice Trees
models.environment_instantiation: event interpretation compatible with ITree-style infrastructure
models.nondeterminism_representation: explicit internal nondeterministic branching distinct from external events
models.comparison_relation: simulation, bisimulation, trace equivalence, and related refinement tools
models.key_distinction: internal choice and environment interaction are represented separately

anneal_design_questions: Who owns each choice: program semantics, environment, or both?
Which traces/state changes/errors/divergence modes are observable to the theorem?
What relation, handler, protocol, or assumption defines admissible outcomes?
Which refinement direction is required across Rust, LLBC, generated Lean, and proof semantics?
Are unsupported effects rejected or preserved as explicit assumptions/effects rather than silently determinized?
